clue.text: Colourless liquid, while in palm, spilt

indicators.note: in signals the word for while sitting inside the jumbled palm
spilt suggests the letters of palm tipped out and lying in a new order

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I spoke'

explanation.surface: Someone holding a clear liquid in a cupped hand lets it run through their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'palm' looks like the hand holding the liquid, but it is anagram fodder: 'spilt' scrambles it to PLMA, and 'in' sets the word for while inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood plasma is the clear, straw-tinted fluid left when the cells are removed, so it is a nearly colourless liquid.

indicators.note: inspiring, literally breathing in, has the song take a letter inside it

parts.note: a lied is a German art song

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word devotion

explanation.surface: A hymn that stirs piety ended up governing someone's life.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIED is a German art song, as by Schubert; 'inspiring' puts N, the last letter of devotion, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled paper has printed lines across it, so lined paper and ruled paper are the same thing.

definitions.meaning: slang for dazed or in a drugged daze
read literally, things set two metres apart have been ..., as in social distancing

explanation.surface: Someone is dazed, maybe from keeping their distance from everyone during a pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading recalls the two-metre social distancing rule of the Covid years.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupefied means dazed and unable to think, which is the slang sense of being in a dreamy, absent state.

clue.text: Out of bounds, large American giant

indicators.note: out of bounds here means the word large loses its outer letters, its boundaries

explanation.surface: A huge American is told he has strayed somewhere off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' strips L and E from large, leaving ARG. Argus Panoptes was the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Argus was a monstrous watchman with a hundred eyes, a giant set to guard Io.

clue.text: Sweep past back of hulking manor

indicators.note: past puts the sweep word after the selected letter
back of selects the final letter of hulking

parts.note: a range is a sweep or extent, as in a sweep of country

explanation.surface: Someone hurries by the rear of a hulking country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' places RANGE after G, the back of hulking.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings, the kind of estate home also called a manor.

parts.note: to part is to leave or depart, that is to go
a wizard casts spells, so might be called a speller, as might one who is a wizard at spelling

explanation.surface: A clergyman is said to be something of a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' is a verb, depart; the question mark flags the whimsical SPELLER for wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospeller is one who reads or preaches the Gospel, an evangelist or preacher.

clue.text: Firstly, all those extra unwanted parcels put away

indicators.note: firstly asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Surplus unwanted parcels are all being stored somewhere out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firstly' takes the initials of the next five words.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is an idiom for eating a lot of it, which is what consuming it greedily means.

definitions.meaning: to ... a place is to cross it from side to side
to ... papers is to examine them carefully

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest cross-examine, a courtroom questioning, but they are two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses use the phrasal verb: traversing a space, and inspecting something item by item.

definitions.meaning: a strong distilled alcoholic drink such as gin or whisky

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a branded energy drink, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit covers both liveliness of temperament and distilled liquor like brandy or rum.

indicators.note: judging by one's ear means going by how a word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a brooch is an ornamental pin used to fasten clothing

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a clip worn near their ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by one's ear' signals a word that sounds the same: BROOCH and BROACH are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it for discussion, that is to bring it up or mention it.

clue.text: Chinese native characters on outskirts of Philadelphia, for example

indicators.note: on here sets the linking word between the two edge letters, which sit on either side of it
outskirts of points to the outer letters of the city name, at its two edges

parts.note: the characters are the two edge letters, read aloud as a pair joined by a conjunction

explanation.surface: A Chinese immigrant lives on the edge of Philadelphia, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The characters on the outskirts of Philadelphia are 'P and A', read out as a phrase; 'for example' marks the panda as one example of a native animal of China.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is found in the wild only in the mountains of central China, so it is a native creature there.

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
an eater is an apple grown for eating raw rather than cooking

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget slices up an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'eater', short for eating apple, is a dessert apple as opposed to a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas heater is a household appliance that warms a room by burning gas.

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
to dress a wound is to bandage it

explanation.surface: A cure involves binding up a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is the setting right of a wrong, a remedy or compensation for it.

clue.text: Shops show work by the setter retrospectively

indicators.note: retrospectively, looking back, has the string of pieces read from the end

parts.note: to air something is to show or display it
op is short for opus, a work
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: Stores put on a display of the compiler's output, looking back over the career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' reverses AIR OP ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large store selling many kinds of goods.

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching an adjective meaning relating to barbers

indicators.note: trained suggests letters drilled into a new formation

explanation.surface: A sailor with no training at cutting hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges SAILOR and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial means relating to barbers and their work, from Latin tonsor, a barber.

definitions.meaning: in folklore a ... was a monster or evil spirit that sat on sleepers
read as ..., a mare being a female horse

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in dread at a monstrous female beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Three readings: the old demon of folklore, a mare that comes at night, and an ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream or terrible experience, earlier the evil spirit (the 'mare') believed to cause it.

clue.text: Rough luck initially filling in binder

indicators.note: filling has that letter fill a gap inside the binder word

parts.note: cement is a binder holding bricks or stones together

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word luck

explanation.surface: Bad luck at first, caught up in a ring binder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binder' suggests a ring folder, but here it is the building material that binds bricks; 'filling' marks the first letter of luck going into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is harsh and stormy, the rough conditions sailors fear.

parts.note: to do a task is to complete it
ugh is the cry of disgust at something gross

explanation.surface: A deal is concluded for a disgustingly large sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like the before-tax sum, beside money; it is disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is long-standing slang for money or cash.

parts.note: drops means falls
a cone is an ice cream served in a wafer cone

explanation.surface: A dessert tumbles onto someone's ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small thick pancake, a teatime griddle cake.

definitions.meaning: one of a person's two hands is the ... one

explanation.definitionFit: Right is both what is morally fair and one of the two sides of the body.

clue.text: Frenchman clothes a gentleman in French label again

indicators.note: clothes means dresses, with the name wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, the French form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman dresses a gentleman in French clothing with a new label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' puts A and M inside RENE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rename something is to give it a new name, to label it a second time.

clue.text: Large vessel: fish nets I say on one

indicators.note: nets means catches, holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
gosh and I say are both mild exclamations of surprise
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A big boat hauls in fish, and someone exclaims about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' is an old-fashioned British exclamation of surprise, here standing for another such cry; 'nets' signals the fish wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo ship is a large freighter carrying goods by sea.

definitions.meaning: a mint is a large sum of money
a paper or card wrapping holding goods

explanation.surface: A sweet comes in a paper wrapper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a peppermint in its wrapper; 'Mint' is a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for a lot of money; a packet is also a small parcel or pack.
A notable is a well-known figure; split in two it describes someone lacking ability.

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or told, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: Word has it that a leg or arm at the front was involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals a homophone: the ship's BOW rhymes with cow, like BOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A bough is a main branch of a tree, called a limb in the same way.

clue.text: As a siren going off, head for cover

definitions.note: As is the chemical symbol, so it stands for the element

indicators.note: going off describes the siren's letters setting off in a new arrangement
head for picks the first letter of cover

explanation.surface: As an alarm sounds, people run for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link word but is the definition. 'going off' makes RSENI from SIREN.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of the poisonous element number 33.

indicators.note: featuring in means the answer appears within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter appears in a photograph belonging to grandma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler, as is usual in crosswords; here it is something that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly that sets around cold meat or eggs, so it is a setting agent.

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the present, matching the third-person verb

parts.note: N is for the North Pole
ears are a pair of sense organs

explanation.surface: A Polish man with a pair of sensors is drawing close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a person from Poland; it is the North Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to come close to it, to approach.

definitions.meaning: taken literally, to measure height is to measure upwards
to cut it is to be good enough

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure up is to meet the required standard, just as to cut it is to be adequate.

parts.note: clip means speed, as in going at a fair clip, so a rate

explanation.surface: Someone talks in an old film clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clip' looks like a snippet of film; it means pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak formally, to deliver a speech.

definitions.meaning: a chilli is literally red and hot

explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot describes something extremely popular, and literally a fiery red chilli pepper.

indicators.note: by puts the revolutionary beside the cycled word, in front

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: cycles means the word see goes round, its last letter coming to the front

explanation.surface: A rider watches bicycles pass a wheel made by a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycles' moves the last letter of see round to the front, giving ESE; 'wheel' is the definition, not part of the cycling picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole round cheese, as made by a cheesemaker, is called a wheel.
